classification_rules.forbidden: must not include, exclude, reorder or replace any headline case

exclusions.reason: Node 22 incompatibility: 'Cannot set property closed of #<Readable> which has only a getter'. Reproduced at both 2019 (cb2e7177) and 2022 (05f12a68) revisions. Environment incompatibility, NOT a Rapture limitation.
my model of the defect was wrong: app.use(RegExp) did not match mid-path even on the buggy revision. Dropped rather than reshaped until it failed.
redirect('back') had already been removed at that revision, so the scaffolding modelled an API that no longer existed.
buggy revision correctly returned 413 under the trigger; the fix concerns stream cleanup and may manifest as a hang rather than a distinct bounded status.
INVERTED: the commit deliberately changed the default, so the parent parsed nested bodies correctly (buggy=200, fixed=500). Not a historical bug in the required direction.

with an out-of-range status the buggy revision crashes the process (no bounded HTTP response, status 0, no artifact); with a near-valid status both revisions normalize identically. No bounded discriminating failure found.

external_validity_note.finding: the fresh corpus is dominated by LOGIC_ONLY_OR_TRIGGER_DOMINANT incidents; most supported cases captured 0 boundary events and none captured pg or outbound-HTTP state
external_validity_note.why_it_matters: an executable incident's distinctive value is reproducing state an agent cannot otherwise obtain. A corpus of logic/trigger-dominant bugs tests the thesis in the regime where .repro adds least.
external_validity_note.why_it_was_not_corrected: preferring stateful bugs is NOT a preregistered inclusion criterion; adding it would bias selection toward the treatment arm. Recorded as a limitation instead of fixed by selection.
